newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa golds slide on Q1 worries, U.S. rate fear.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa golds slide on Q1 worries, U.S. rate fear.

text.p: Anxiety over expected poor first quarter gold results, weak bullion and fears of a U.S. interest rate hike knocked South African gold shares on Monday with Western Areas Gold Mining Co Ltd taking the brunt.
Western Areas fell to a 20-month low of 45 rand a share before inching back up to 45.50 rand, 575 cents lower than open, in a traded volume of 61,600 shares.
The gold index was last 57.1 points down at 1,325.3 points.

Expectations of a disappointing first quarter for gold mines due to a weaker bullion price, stronger rand and four public holidays hitting production was partly to blame for weakness on the gold board, dealers said.
"It's partly due to the fact that results for Q1 are going to be affected by the stronger rand and weaker gold price. They're not going to be good," one dealer said.
The bullion price has been eroded for most of this year and on Monday broke the key $350 an ounce level again to trade last at $349.70/350.20 an ounce.

After last year's 29 percent fall against the dollar, the rand has since firmed and was last bid at 4.4280 on the dollar. A stronger rand does not bode well for local gold companies, shrinking their export dollar earnings.

Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting at which Governor Alan Greenspan is widely expected to hike U.S. interest rates -- a blow to bullion -- was another culprit blamed for triggering anxiety and knocking gold shares, dealers said.
"There is the fear that if there is a U.S. interest rate hike then this doesn't exactly help gold," another dealer said.
But market expectations are that if rates rise it will likely be by 0.25 or 0.5 percentage points and much of this has already been discounted.
Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd lost 150 cents to 33.50 rand, Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd shed 14.25 rand to 278 rand and Kloof Gold Mining Co Ltd cut 145 cents to 32.75 rand.
